Novatian
noh-VAY-shun
proper noun
From the Latin name Novatianus, a learned presbyter of Rome in the third century, author of an orthodox treatise on the Trinity but the founder of a rigorist schism.

Biblical Definition

Novatian was a learned presbyter of the church at Rome in the middle of the third century, and the first Roman theologian to write in Latin. His treatise On the Trinity is a sound and able defence of the orthodox doctrine of the Godhead, and for this the dictionary gives him his due. But his name is fixed in the memory of the church for a grievous error. When the great persecution had passed, and many who had lapsed under torture sought to return with tears to the communion of the church, Novatian held that the church had no power to receive them, and that the gravely fallen could never again be admitted to the Lord’s table though they repented. Refusing the bishop chosen at Rome, he set himself up as a rival and gathered a sect that bore his name and lasted for centuries. The dictionary names this rigorism as a corruption of the gospel. Scripture commands that a man overtaken in a fault be restored in the spirit of meekness (Gal 6:1), that the penitent be forgiven and comforted lest he be swallowed up of overmuch sorrow (2Co 2:7), and assures that if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive (1Jo 1:9). A purity that denies repentance to the fallen is not holiness but cruelty, and unsays the very gospel it pretends to guard.

Webster 1828 Definition

A third-century Roman presbyter, orthodox on the Trinity but founder of a rigorist schism denying restoration to the lapsed.

expand to see more

NOVATIAN, a learned presbyter of Rome in the middle of the third century.

He was the first Roman theologian to write in Latin.

His treatise On the Trinity is a sound defence of orthodoxy.

He denied that the church could restore the gravely lapsed who repented.

He set up a rival bishopric and founded the rigorist Novatian sect.

Key Scripture

Gal 6:1 — "Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted."

2Co 2:7 — "So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow."

1Jo 1:9 — "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness."

Mat 18:22 — "Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven."

Modern Corruption

His rigorism denied the penitent lapsed any return, a cruelty that unsays the gospel of grace it claimed to guard.

expand to see more

The corruption to name is Novatianism, the rigorist error that the church has no power to restore the gravely fallen, even when they return in true repentance. Born of a zeal for purity in the wake of persecution, it hardened into a schism that refused the penitent the comfort of the gospel and shut the door that Christ Himself had opened. The dictionary names it plainly as a departure from the grace of God.

Scripture is decisive against it. The spiritual are to restore the one overtaken in a fault; the penitent is to be forgiven and comforted; the Lord bids us forgive until seventy times seven. A holiness that denies repentance to the fallen is no true holiness but a cruelty, and it betrays a low view of the blood of Christ, as though some sins lay beyond its cleansing. Novatian’s sound doctrine of the Trinity could not save a sect founded upon a denial of grace; and his error stands as a warning that purity divorced from mercy becomes itself a corruption of the gospel.

Hebrew Roots

From the Latin Novatianus, the name marks a third-century Roman theologian and the founder of a rigorist schism.

Novatian — Latin Novatianus, a presbyter of Rome.

He flourished in the middle of the third century.

He wrote a sound treatise On the Trinity.

He denied restoration to the gravely lapsed who repented.

He founded the rigorist sect that bore his name.

Usage

"Like Novatian’s error, a purity that denies repentance to the fallen unsays the gospel of grace."

"Restore the one overtaken in a fault in the spirit of meekness, lest he be swallowed of sorrow."

"No sin of the penitent lies beyond the cleansing of the blood of Christ."
